title: French method books and Solfege
summary: His stolen Clodomir method and solfege books, and what music is.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: What were your exercise books that you had? Well, I had a French book that someone stole from.

It was called the Clodermier. C-L-O-U-D-M-I-E-R. It's the old French method. And it had everything in it. It had, from the beginning, the whole notes, then the half notes, then the quarter notes, and so forth and so on. And there were a lot of solos in there that were taken from Poet and Peasant and these other things like that. But this book was stolen from me and I've never been able to get another one like it. And just like my Sol Fage book that I learned to sing the notes and the music too, those were stolen from me. And I've never been able to get another one like it. I can't think of the name of it. All this was old French methods.
A lot of people use Italian Sol Feds.

Yeah, over here. Pascal Bono. Right, right. They all are basically the same. In fact, it is basically the same. Now that the print might be a little different. Or maybe some of the notes might, I mean, the formation of the notes might look a little different. But basically it is the Sol Feds is the same way anywhere you're going. It's the beginning of music, what music is. And a lot of these fellas there, you tell them Sol Feds, they don't know what you're talking about. You ask them what is music, they can't answer you. Because they don't know. And when you tell a guy, music is a combination of sounds that are pleasing to the ear.

Then he couldn't explain it to you because here's a damn show not pleasing to the ear. When he's going to play all these loud noises on the guitars and on that electric bass, then it ceases to become music. Yeah.
